chunks: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali b. Ibrahim narrated to us from his father, from Yusuf b. Aqil, from Ishaq b. Rahuwayh. He said: When Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) arrived in Nishapur and wanted to depart from it toward al-Ma'mun, the people of hadith gathered around him and said to him: 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, you depart from us without narrating a hadith that we may benefit from?' He had been sitting in the howdah, so he raised his head and said: 'I heard my father Musa b. Ja'far say: I heard my father Ja'far b. Muhammad say: I heard my father Muhammad b. Ali say: I heard my father Ali b. al-Husayn say: I heard my father al-Husayn b. Ali say: I heard my father, the Commander of the Believers, Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them all) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) say: I heard Gabriel (peace be upon him) say: I heard Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, say:
'There is no god but Allah' is My fortress; whoever enters My fortress is safe from My punishment.
When the caravan continued on, he called out to us: 'With its conditions, and I am among its conditions.'

key_terms.الْعِمَارِيَّة: Howdah - a covered litter or seat mounted on a camel for travel
key_terms.حِصْنِي: My fortress - a metaphor for divine protection through the declaration of monotheism (tawhid)
key_terms.سِلْسِلَة الذَّهَب: The Golden Chain - this hadith is famous for its unbroken chain of transmission through all the Imams
key_terms.شُرُوطِهَا: Its conditions - referring to the prerequisites of the testimony of faith, which include recognizing the Imamate

ai.seo_question: What is the Hadith of the Golden Chain (Silsilat al-Dhahab) narrated by Imam al-Rida in Nishapur?
ai.summary: This is the celebrated Hadith al-Silsila al-Dhahab (Hadith of the Golden Chain), one of the most famous narrations in Shia Islam. Imam al-Rida transmitted it through an unbroken chain of the Twelve Imams going back through the Prophet to Gabriel to Allah Himself, declaring that the testimony of faith is a divine fortress of safety. The Imam's addendum 'and I am among its conditions' emphasizes that true monotheism requires recognition of the divinely appointed Imamate.
word_analysis: may Allah have mercy on him
